measured_by: read-only requests against the canonical endpoint; no billable tool was called

canonical.note: This is the only address that ever receives the user's key. Every field is pinned in the schema and re-checked by the validator (no userinfo, no port, no query, no fragment) because a silent edit here would exfiltrate credentials. Both /mcp and /mcp/ are accepted by the server; a client that fails on one has a client-side URL-handling fault, not a server fault.

credential.evidence: 401 body: "Authentication required. Provide an sk_ or lce_ API key as Bearer token."
credential.note: Both prefixes are valid. A check that demands sk_ rejects real keys.

unauthenticated.note: Every MCP method is auth-gated. An expected 401 is therefore a credential-free proof that the endpoint is reachable and speaking.

fingerprint.observed: Bearer realm="OAuth", resource_metadata="https://api.superdocs.app/mcp/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource", error="invalid_token", error_description="Missing or invalid access token"
fingerprint.purpose: Distinguishes a genuine SuperDocs 401 from a corporate proxy or captive portal returning 401/407. Without it, a network interception is misdiagnosed as a bad key.

discovery.purpose: An unambiguous, machine-readable liveness probe that needs no credential, and the authoritative URL to cite when telling a developer where to obtain a key.

accept_header.rejected_body_contains: Not Acceptable: Client must accept application/js
accept_header.note: A wildcard is NOT sufficient. Absent, */* and text/html all return 406. Modern streamable-HTTP clients sending 'application/json, text/event-stream' are accepted.

protocol.doctor_rule: NEVER diagnose a protocol version as a fault. Send initialize, read result.protocolVersion, report it as an observation. The server negotiates; treating a version as broken would send a developer to change a working configuration.

session.note: Stateless at the transport layer. Tolerate a session header if one appears in future rather than assuming its absence forever.

handshake.note: The canonical authenticated sequence used for the connected check.

inventory.note: Dated observation. A difference is reported as profile drift and never fails a working connection.
